small_guidance:
- Remove the explicit `BLOCK=1024` kwarg at the launch site of `_mean_kernel` since `BLOCK` is already an autotuned symbol; also drop the conflicting `num_warps=4` kwarg (autotune sets it). Just call `_mean_kernel[grid](y, m, HW, y.stride(0), y.stride(1), OC)`.
- Pass `OC` as a positional argument matching the kernel signature (currently the call passes `BLOCK=` but the kernel signature has `OC` before `BLOCK`); reorder args to match.
- Consider adding configs with BLOCK=16384 num_warps=8 for HW=262144 (514×514) since the reduction axis is large.
large_guidance:
- The conv_transpose dominates runtime here (16×128×514×514 output from a 3×3 transposed conv on 16×64×512×512). Tuning the mean/LSE tail will not move the needle while torch's ConvTranspose2d runs unfused. Replace it with a custom Triton scatter-add ConvTranspose2d kernel (one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), scatter input×weight outer products), and fuse the global-mean reduction directly into the conv epilogue so the full N×OC×H×W tensor is never materialized.
- Better: since the only consumer of the conv output is a global mean over (H,W), fuse conv-transpose with an accumulator that sums each output element into a per-(N,OC) register/atomic accumulator — but this must still perform the full IC×kh×kw×H_out×W_out multiply-adds (no pre-summing weight along kh,kw or input along H,W). Each output position's value must be computed in full before contributing to the sum.
- After the fused conv+mean produces the (N,OC) tensor, keep the existing small LSE kernel; that part is already negligible. The redesign's leverage is entirely in the conv replacement.
